jobs.title: Robotics Research Scientist (San Francisco, CA)
jobs.description:
### **About Tutor**

We believe robots are the biggest lever we have to making the physical world a better, more affordable place. But robots are a rounding error in our society: nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t even have a single robot, and robots have yet to make their way into our homes or places of business.

Tutor Intelligence is changing that.

Tutor is a robotics research and deployment company, building generally capable robot hardware and artificial intelligence to enable robots to go where no robots have gone before. Sonny is a semi-humanoid robot with frontier dexterity approaching the human form. Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for businesses from family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Tutor robots are manufactured at scale and operate as a network, combining the whole fleet’s learned experience to train ever more capable robot artificial intelligence.

Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, our team is full stack: we design and manufacture robot hardware, train our own models, work directly with the smallest and largest end-customers, and maintain our fleet across the United States. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.

Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.

### **The Role**

Are you tired of writing incremental code for massive CRUD web-apps? Do you want to build systems from the ground up that effect change in the physical world, not just the digital one? At Tutor, we are motivated by ***atoms not electrons***: every line of code you write has a real world impact at the foundation of our global economy, solving the core technical problems to evolve humanity and society to the next level.

Tutor Intelligence builds software to enable ordinary robots to achieve extraordinary things. As a research scientist, your work lies at the center of this challenge, building the AI algorithms and systems that drive novel capabilities in the lab and in the field.

At the core, we are looking for motivated and curious individuals who have exceptionally strong programming fundamentals. Experience in specific technical stacks or with robotics/ML are helpful but not requirements: whatever shape your skill set is, Tutor engineers and researchers shape their own roles to best tackle the frontier of robotics development.

### **Requirements**

* Exceptionally strong programming skills and comfort in one or more programming languages
* Natural collaborator, excited to work closely around a whiteboard in a team setting
* Excited by the future full of robots and a reshaped physical economy
* Not afraid to step foot in a factory or a warehouse

### **Nice to haves (zero or more)**

* Advanced proficiency with Python and/or Typescript + React
* Experience with robot arms / manipulation
* Experience with motion planning and robot optimization
* Experience with perception or computer vision (deep or classical)
* Experience with infra and devtools (systemd, Docker, Kubernetes)
* Experience with hardware / software integration

### **Why Tutor?**

Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.

Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.

### **Benefits**

We take care of our team so they can do their best work. At Tutor, you’ll get:

* Fully employer-covered health insurance, so you’re protected without the premium.
* A managed 401(k) to help you plan for the future.
* Generous time off: unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees.
* Regular in-office meals and team social events throughout the year.

As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.

Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.

jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist
jobs.description:
Requisition ID # 175422
  
  
**Job Category:** Engineering / Science
  
**Job Level:** Individual Contributor
  
**Business Unit:** Energy Delivery
  
**Work Type:** Hybrid
  
**Job Location:** Danville; San Ramon
  
  
Department Overview
  
Electric Transmission & Distribution ensures the delivery of clean, safe, reliable and affordable energy to nearly 16 million people in Northern and Central California. The Electric Transmission & Distribution Team is responsible for ensuring the electric grid's reliability and resiliency through the ongoing maintenance and operations of PG&E's 100,000 miles of distribution lines and over 18,000 miles of Transmission lines. Coworkers in Electric Transmission & Distribution actively engage in the Lean Methodology through the use of visual management in operating reviews to cross-functionally identify and solve problems, and create standard work. By working together as One Electric. One Team. We are delivering for our hometowns. Electric Transmission & Distribution is comprised of approximately 6,500 coworkers.
  
  
Position Summary
  
The Applied Technology Services (ATS) staff provides advanced analytical, modeling, testing, and risk assessment services across multiple disciplines to support company organizations in identifying, quantifying, and addressing complex operational and asset-related risks. The team develops and applies statistical, probabilistic, and machine learning-based approaches to evaluate system performance, asset condition, degradation trends, and probability of failure, enabling data-driven decision making for reliability, resilience, and lifecycle management.
  
  
Staff integrate and analyze diverse data sources to develop predictive models, risk metrics, and analytical tools that support asset strategy, maintenance planning, investment prioritization, and operational decision making. Services include asset health assessments, reliability and risk evaluations, failure investigations, scenario analyses, and development of quantitative methodologies for complex infrastructure systems, including transmission and distribution assets, distributed energy resources, and generation facilities.
  
  
The team provides technical consultation and analytical insights to internal clients, helping organizations proactively manage risk and improve asset performance through the application of advanced modeling techniques, data analytics, and industry best practices. Staff collaborate with business and technical stakeholders to develop analytical solutions, support project proposals, and communicate complex model results and risk insights to decision makers. Incumbents maintain knowledge of and adhere to all company and regulatory safety, quality, and governance requirements.
  
  
This position is hybrid, working from your remote office and your assigned work location based on business need.
  
  
The selected candidate must live within PG&E’s service territory.
  
  
PG&E is providing the salary range that the company in good faith believes it might pay for this position at the time of the job posting. This compensation range is specific to the locality of the job. The actual salary paid to an individual will be based on multiple factors, including, but not limited to, specific skills, education, licenses or certifications, experience, market value, geographic location, and internal equity. Although we estimate the successful candidate hired into this role will be placed towards the middle or entry point of the range, the decision will be made on a case-by-case basis related to these factors.​
  
  
**A reasonable salary range is:**  
Minimum Base Salary (Bay Area) $126,000.00
  
Mid Base Salary (Bay Area) $163,000.00
  
Maximum Base Salary (Bay Area) $200,000.00
  
  
Job Responsibilities Researches and applies knowledge of existing and emerging data science principles, theories, and techniques to inform business decisions. Creates data mining architectures / models / protocols, statistical reporting, and data analysis methodologies to identify trends in structured and unstructured data sets. Extracts, transforms, and loads data from dissimilar sources from across PG&E for their machine learning feature engineering. Applies data science/ machine learning /artificial intelligence methods to develop defensible and reproducible predictive or optimization models, Co-develops mathematical models and AI simulations that represent complex business problems. Writes and documents python code for data science (feature engineering and machine learning modeling) independently. Develops and presents summary presentations to business. Develops statistical, probabilistic, and machine learning models for asset condition assessment, degradation analysis, probability of failure estimation, and risk quantification to support risk-informed decision making. Develops and maintains probability of failure models, risk metrics, and analytical tools using asset condition, inspection, operational, environmental, and historical performance data to support asset strategy, reliability, maintenance, and lifecycle decisions. Performs model evaluation, sensitivity and scenario analyses, and quantification of uncertainty, and communicates model results, assumptions, failure drivers, and risk insights to engineering, asset management, operational, and business stakeholders.
  
  
Qualifications
  
Minimum Bachelor’s Degree in Data Science, Machine Learning, Computer Science, Physics, Econometrics or Economics, Engineering, Mathematics, Applied Sciences, Statistics, or equivalent field. 4 years in data science (or 2 years, if possess Master’s Degree, as described above).
  
  
**Desired:** Master’s Degree in Data Science, Machine Learning, Computer Science, Physics, Econometrics or Economics, Engineering, Mathematics, Applied Sciences, Statistics, or equivalent field. ambiguous_jobs.title: Staff AI Scientist (Fintech Risk AI/ML)
ambiguous_jobs.description:
**Overview**
------------

**The team**
------------

Money Movement Risk AI/ML is a team of AI scientists and ML engineers in Intuit's Fintech Risk organization. Our models decide, in real time, whether money moves for small businesses on QuickBooks: card and ACH payments, money coming in, money going out, when funds are released, and how long a payment is held.

Every decision has two failure modes. Approve the wrong transaction and Intuit takes a fraud or credit loss. Decline or hold the right one and a small business waits for money it has already earned. Our job is to push both down at the same time.

Our mandate: **AI touches every money movement risk decision.** That covers deciding (authorize, fund, release), acting on the decision (queue, investigate, hold), and accounting for it (expected loss).

**The role**
------------

You will be the technical owner of one money movement risk capability: its models, its evaluation, its production health, and its business outcome. You will design, train, validate, and ship the models yourself, and you will set direction for the scientists and engineers who build with you.

This role is for an AI producer. You will build new models from first principles and put them in front of live money. It is not a role for wiring an existing LLM into a product surface.

**What you will work on**
-------------------------

Depending on fit and team needs, you will own one or more of these areas:

* **Authorization risk.** Real-time fraud and loss models that approve, decline, or step up card and ACH transactions, for both money coming in and money going out.
* **Funding and settlement risk.** Models that decide when funds are released and how long payments are held or delayed, so good customers get paid faster and risky payments are caught before money leaves.
* **Balance and account-level money risk.** Risk on stored balances and on the accounts behind them, as more money stays inside Intuit.
* **Day-1 risk for new money products.** Risk decisioning that is ready when a new payment or funding product launches, often with almost no labeled history.
* **Agentic money movement.** Transaction risk for payments and money actions initiated by AI agents and assistants: agent identity, consent, and intent.
* **Risk-ranked queueing.** Ranking cases for risk operations by dollars at risk, so analysts spend time where the loss is.

**Responsibilities**

**What you will do**
--------------------

* **Own outcomes, not just models.** Define success in loss, approval rate, hold rate, and time-to-funds. Ship models that move those numbers, and own them in production.
* **Solve the hard statistics of risk.** Delayed and noisy labels (chargebacks and returns arrive weeks later), extreme class imbalance, and selection bias from models whose decisions shape their own training data. Use holdouts, reject inference, and counterfactual evaluation to measure what actually happened.
* **Build for adaptive adversaries.** Detect fraud rings, account takeover, and new attack patterns with graph, sequence, and anomaly-detection methods. Test models against attackers who probe, retry, and adapt.
* **Make models production-grade.** Partner with ML engineers on real-time features, low-latency serving, automated retraining, and monitoring for drift, data quality, and loss.
* **Turn Intuit's data into an advantage.** Build reusable, versioned features and labels from transaction, account, and network data that other models on the team can build on.
* **Set the evaluation bar.** Establish offline and online evaluation, experimentation, and adversarial testing standards for your area.
* **Lead across functions.** Work with risk policy, product, engineering, risk operations, and finance. Explain trade-offs between loss and friction in plain terms and drive decisions.
* **Raise the team.** Mentor senior and early-career scientists and engineers, lead design and model reviews, and help hire.

**Qualifications**

**What you bring**
------------------

**Required**

* 8+ years building and deploying ML models in production, including significant work in fraud, payments, credit, or another adversarial or financial-risk domain.
* MS or PhD in Statistics, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Operations Research, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* A track record of owning models that made real-time, high-stakes decisions, with measured business impact.
* Deep expertise in gradient-boosted trees, deep learning, and anomaly detection, plus the statistics to validate them: calibration, imbalance, delayed labels, and selection bias.
* Strong Python and SQL, and hands-on large-scale feature engineering with Spark or similar.
* Experience shipping models with ML engineers: real-time features, serving, retraining, monitoring.
* Sound experimental judgment in a risk setting: A/B tests, holdouts, and their limits when attackers can exploit them.
* Clear communication with risk, product, and business leaders.

**Preferred**

* Payments risk experience: card and ACH authorization, funding, chargebacks, returns, or settlement.
* Graph ML or network analysis for fraud rings and collusion.
* Sequence or representation learning on transaction and behavioral data.
* Experience building or evaluating LLM and agentic systems, especially for risk or operations.
* Model risk management and explainability in a regulated financial-services environment.
* Experience leading a technical area across teams and mentoring scientists.

**Why join**
------------

* **Your work moves real money.** Your models decide whether small businesses get paid, and how fast.
* **Hard problems.** Millisecond decisions, adaptive attackers, labels that arrive weeks late, and models that shape their own training data.
* **Full ownership.** Scientists here own their models from problem framing to production. Nobody hands you a spec.
* **An AI-native risk org.** We are building toward AI making every money movement risk
